prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1481; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss for a low-speed head-on collision. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed into their lane on a curve. Both drivers stated no airbags deployed and both vehicles were driven from the scene. Photos requested from insured and assigned to field appraiser.

Entry 2: Claimant reports neck and shoulder pain and has retained counsel. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Requested signed medical authorization and prior treatment history through counsel. Liability on the other driver appears probable based on the insured's statement and the police report narrative.

Entry 3: Field appraisal completed on both vehicles. Damage is front-end on each, consistent with a low-speed impact. Repair estimates received and under review. Recommended a quick-repair review on the insured vehicle and a supplement check on the claimant's vehicle once teardown is done.

Entry 4: Claimant's counsel submitted treatment records showing a diagnosed shoulder strain with physical therapy ordered. Records reviewed. Requested an independent medical review to confirm causation and reasonableness of the planned care. Reserve adjusted to reflect the bodily injury exposure.

Entry 5: Counsel responded that the claimant is still in active treatment and no settlement demand has been made. Diary set for follow-up in 30 days. Will continue to coordinate repair authorization for the insured vehicle and monitor the independent review for the shoulder claim.
